name: Light Amparo Purple
lede: Light Amparo Purple is a paler reading of [[amparo-purple|Amparo Purple]], a hue Ridgway recorded in his 1912 atlas and the ISCC-NBS system filed again in 1955.

sections.title: A modifier on an undocumented name
sections.body:
The name is built by grammar, "light" plus the parent color [[amparo-purple|Amparo Purple]], whose own name is undocumented in the sources consulted; "Amparo" is a Spanish word for shelter and a common given name, but nothing we hold confirms a link [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas places the parent hue on plate XI, hue 63, and the ISCC-NBS system separately filed it in 1955 as block 217, a brilliant purple [1]. This paler, lighter version keeps the same two-source record [1].

Its nearest named neighbor in the color graph is [[bright-lilac|Bright Lilac]], 3.9 units away, with [[lavender-pink|Lavender Pink]] close behind at 4.1 and [[rose-purple|Rose-Purple]] at 4.2 [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within a color distance of 4, as photographed [2]. A bright, pale modern purple like this, built as a lightened variant rather than drawn from a historical pigment, sits outside the range painters working from natural dyes and earths had on hand [2].
